title: Thame 2024 event evidence workbook
citation: Compiled by the team from the NHESS article (nhess-26-4131-2026), its supplement, UNOSAT LS20240818NPL and Sentinel Asia event page; see the Sources_and_Caveats sheet.

columns.name: Details
examples: Two separate event-level datasets: one for GLOF occurrence and one for satellite-mapped landslide/mudslide impact.
Actual reported values from the uploaded Thame workbook and published Thame event sources are entered where available.
These are event-level records, NOT pixel-level training samples. One positive event does not provide enough independent samples to train or validate a machine-learning classifier.
glof_label = 1 for the documented 16-Aug-2024 Thame GLOF event. No verified non-GLOF/negative samples are present.
landslide_label = 1 for the UNOSAT satellite-mapped landslide/mudslide scar inventory (~140 ha). UNOSAT explicitly marks the assessment preliminary and not field-validated.

records.Details: Two separate event-level datasets: one for GLOF occurrence and one for satellite-mapped landslide/mudslide impact.
Actual reported values from the uploaded Thame workbook and published Thame event sources are entered where available.
These are event-level records, NOT pixel-level training samples. One positive event does not provide enough independent samples to train or validate a machine-learning classifier.
glof_label = 1 for the documented 16-Aug-2024 Thame GLOF event. No verified non-GLOF/negative samples are present.
landslide_label = 1 for the UNOSAT satellite-mapped landslide/mudslide scar inventory (~140 ha). UNOSAT explicitly marks the assessment preliminary and not field-validated.
GLOF flood extent and landslide/mudslide scars are kept as separate target types. A flooded pixel is not automatically labelled as a landslide.

Scene dates, platforms, product descriptions and image resolutions are source-reported. Numeric VV/VH/HH/HV backscatter, coherence, incidence angle and LOS displacement are not published in the source material reviewed.

Reported lake/village elevations, catchment areas, and a localized bedrock-step geometry are included. The source article says it used HMA DEM and a 1 m UAV DEM, but the raster cell values for slope/aspect/curvature/TWI are not in the supplied workbook.
Blank cells mean unavailable/not reported, not zero. Do not replace blanks with zero.

The 39.8° angle in Terrain_Observations is calculated from the paper's reported 100 m vertical drop over 120 m horizontal distance. It is a local steep-section estimate, not a raster-derived slope layer.

Use this workbook as a source-grounded event inventory and data-preparation starting point. Obtain/download the actual raster layers and vector inventories, align them spatially, then create many pixel/grid/slope-unit samples and verified negative samples.
